newsitem.title: JAPAN: NISSAN TO DRASICALLY CUT AUGUST OUTPUT IN THAILAND.
newsitem.headline: NISSAN TO DRASICALLY CUT AUGUST OUTPUT IN THAILAND.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it would drastically cut its output in Thailand in August for inventory adjustment.
Nissan, which has two factories in Thailand, will stop operations for the whole of August at a plant which produces pickup trucks, a Nissan spokesman said.
The other plant, which makes cars, will operate for only six days in August, he said.
He declined to give figures for the two factories' output in recent months or their production capacity.
But he said it would be a drastic cut in production.
The cut was decided to adjust inventories and was not related to economic reform plans that the Thai government announced earlier this week, he said.
"Since the end of last year, sales have been slow and the level of inventories has climbed," the company spokesman said.
He said total vehicle sales in Thailand in the January-June period totalled 248,185 units, down 14.5 percent from the same period a year ago.
Nissan's sales in Thailand in the six-month period were 31,240, down 37.7 percent year-on-year, he said.
Nissan hopes to return to normal operations in Thailand in September but no decision has been made yet, he said.
The spokesman declined to say if Nissan plans take any measures to cope with the effects of Thailand's economic restructuring plans.

On Tuesday, Thailand, in deep recession as a result of the collapse of a real estate and asset "bubble", announced a series of economic reform measures and said it was seeking the loans from foreign countries and the International Monetary Fund to stabilise its economy.
The economic problems in Thailand have prompted other Japanese companies to take a cautious stance on investments there.
